results.title: GPU Prices 2026: H100 From $3.49/hr, RTX 5070 at +58%
results.author: Axis Intelligence Research
highlights:
Our research reports combine primary data analysis, industry surveys, and expert interviews to provide actionable intelligence for technology decision-makers. Each report undergoes peer review by at least two subject-matter

...

By Axis Intelligence Research

Co-author: Sarah Mitchell | Last updated: October 2, 2026 | License: CC BY 4.0

> Prices verified on October 2, 2026. Every price on this page was read from the vendor’s live pricing page, public price API or retail listing on that date. AWS Capacity Block rates effective October 7, 2026 are taken from AWS’s own announcement on its pricing page.

Renting one NVIDIA H100 for an hour costs $3.49 on Runpod and $12.29 on Microsoft Azure — the same chip, listed on public pricing pages on October 2, 2026. Axis Intelligence Research’s GPU Hour Premium Ratio puts the hyperscaler list premium at 2.93x the neocloud median, and AWS is raising every GPU Capacity Block rate by roughly 15% on October 7.

## Quick Answer

How much does a GPU cost in October 2026? In the cloud, an NVIDIA H100 lists between $3.49 and $12.29 per GPU-hour on-demand; the neocloud median is $3.99. A B200 lists from $6.69 to $8.60. On the consumer side, the cheapest new RTX 5070 on Newegg was $869.99 against a $549 launch price — 58% above MSRP.

...

1. According to Axis Intelligence Research, hyperscalers list the NVIDIA H100 at 2.93 times the neocloud median price — $11.68 versus $3.99 per GPU-hour on-demand, as of October 2, 2026 (GPU Hour Premium Ratio, GHPR).
2. AWS raises EC2 Capacity Block GPU rates about 15% effective October 7, 2026, taking an H100 accelerator-hour from $5.191 to $5.970 and a B200 from $12.355 to $14.208, per AWS’s pricing page.
3. An 8-GPU H100 server rented on-demand for three years costs $2.58 million on Azure and $734,000 on Runpod, according to Axis Intelligence Research’s list-price TCO calculation.
4. The cheapest new GeForce RTX 5070 on Newegg cost $869.99 on October 2, 2026, 58% above the $549 price NVIDIA announced at CES in January 2025.
5. Azure’s spot price for an 8x H100 VM is 82% below its own on-demand rate — $18.17 versus $98.32 per hour in US East, per Microsoft’s Retail Prices API.

...

### H100 on-demand price per GPU-hour by provider (October 2, 2026)

| Provider | Instance / SKU | Listed price | GPUs | Price per GPU-hour | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Runpod | H100 SXM Pod (Secure Cloud) | $3.49/hr | 1 | $3.49 | Runpod pricing |
| Lambda | NVIDIA H100 SXM instance | $3.99/GPU/hr | 1–8 | $3.99 | Lambda pricing |
| CoreWeave | NVIDIA HGX H100 (North America) | $49.24/hr | 8 | $6.16 | CoreWeave pricing |
| Google Cloud | a3-highgpu-8g, us-central1 | $88.49/hr | 8 | $11.06 | Google Cloud accelerator-optimized pricing |
| Microsoft Azure | ND96isr H100 v5, East US | $98.32/hr | 8 | $12.29 | Azure Retail Prices API |

Per-GPU-hour figures for 8-GPU instances are Axis Intelligence Research calculations: instance price ÷ 8. Google Cloud and Azure prices include the host vCPUs, memory and local SSD bundled into the VM; neocloud prices also bundle host resources, but in smaller amounts per GPU.

The spread from cheapest to most expensive is 3.5x ($12.29 ÷ $3.49). That is the number most “GPU price” pages quote, and it overstates the useful comparison, because Runpod’s $3.49 Pod and Azure’s $98.32 VM are not the same product. Azure sells an eight-GPU VM with its host CPU, memory and storage bundled in; a single Pod is a single GPU.

...

AWS’s per-accelerator figure that we verified is the EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML rate — a reservation you book for a fixed window, not open-ended on-demand. On October 2, 2026 the p5.48xlarge (8x H100) Capacity Block rate in US East (N. Virginia) was $41.528 per instance-hour, or $5.191 per H100. AWS’s pricing page states that from October 7, 2026, the P5 rate becomes $5.970 per accelerator across all available regions. Axis Intelligence Research did not verify a current AWS on-demand p5 rate for this snapshot, so AWS is excluded from the on-demand table rather than estimated.

## Why Is AWS Raising GPU Prices in October 2026?

AWS publishes the reason in one line: Capacity Block reservation prices are dynamic and are updated periodically based on supply and demand. The October 7, 2026 update moves every GPU family up by the same proportion.

### AWS EC2 Capacity Block rate change, effective October 7, 2026

| Instance family | GPU | Rate before (per accelerator-hour) | Rate from Oct 7, 2026 | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P6-B300 | B300 | $14.040 | $16.146 | +15.0% |
| P6-B200 | B200 | $12.355 | $14.208 | +15.0% |
| P5en | H200 | $6.865 | $7.895 | +15.0% |
| P5e | H200 | $5.970 | $6.866 | +15.0% |
| P5 | H100 | $5.191 | $5.970 | +15.0% |
| P4de | A100 80GB | $2.214 | $2.546 | +15.0% |
| P4d | A100 40GB | $1.475 | $1.696 | +15.0% |

Source: AWS EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML pricing, retrieved October 2, 2026. “Before” rates are the US East (N. Virginia) or US-region rates listed on the same page; percentage change is an Axis Intelligence Research calculation.

A uniform 15% move across seven GPU generations — including a 2020-era A100 40GB — tells you this is not a scarcity signal about one chip. Capacity Blocks are AWS’s mechanism for guaranteed short-term cluster access, and a flat repricing across the whole catalog reads as AWS re-pricing guaranteed availability itself. Buyers who only need interruptible capacity should read this as a reason to look at spot and neocloud rates, not as proof that GPUs in general got 15% more expensive.

## How Much Does a B200 or H200 Cost per Hour?

### Blackwell and H200 per-GPU-hour prices (October 2, 2026)

| GPU | Provider | Pricing model | Price per GPU-hour | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B200 | Lambda | On-demand instance | $6.69 | Lambda pricing |
| B200 | Runpod | On-demand Pod | $6.79 | Runpod pricing |
| B200 | CoreWeave | On-demand, 8x HGX ($68.80/hr) | $8.60 | CoreWeave pricing |
| B200 | Lambda | 1-Click Cluster, 256+ GPUs, 2 weeks–1 year | $8.87 | Lambda pricing |
| B200 | Google Cloud | DWS Flex-start, a4-highgpu-8g ($64.44/hr) | $8.06 | Google Cloud pricing |
| B200 | AWS | Capacity Block, from Oct 7, 2026 | $14.21 | AWS pricing |
| B300 | Runpod | On-demand Pod | $7.89 | Runpod pricing |
| H200 | Runpod | On-demand Pod | $4.59 | Runpod pricing |
| H200 | CoreWeave | On-demand, 8x HGX ($50.44/hr) | $6.31 | CoreWeave pricing |
| H200 | Google Cloud | On-demand, a3-ultragpu-8g ($84.81/hr) | $10.60 | Google Cloud pricing |

One detail that most rate cards hide: Lambda’s B200 is cheaper on-demand ($6.69) than in its own 1-Click Clusters ($8.87–$9.86). The cluster price buys guaranteed multi-node capacity with interconnect, not a per-GPU discount. Google Cloud does not list an on-demand price for its A4 (B200) VM at all; the cheapest public path is DWS Flex-start at $64.44 per 8-GPU hour.

...

### H100 price per GPU-hour by commitment model (October 2, 2026)

| Provider | Model | Price per GPU-hour | vs. same provider on-demand |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Azure (East US) | On-demand | $12.29 | — |
| Azure (East US) | 1-year reservation ($551,221 per VM) | $7.87 | −36% |
| Azure (East US) | 3-year reservation ($1,134,310 per VM) | $5.40 | −56% |
| Azure (East US) | Spot ($18.17/hr per VM) | $2.27 | −82% |
| Google Cloud (us-central1) | On-demand | $11.06 | — |
| Google Cloud | 1-year resource CUD | $7.67 | −31% |
| Google Cloud | 3-year resource CUD | $4.86 | −56% |
| Google Cloud | DWS Flex-start | $4.79 | −57% |
| Google Cloud | Spot | $6.62 | −40% |
| CoreWeave | Spot ($19.71/hr per 8 GPUs) | $2.46 | −60% |

Per-GPU-hour = VM price ÷ 8. Azure reservation per-hour = total term price ÷ (term years × 8,760 hours) ÷ 8. All Axis Intelligence Research calculations from vendor list prices.

...

### Will AWS GPU prices go up in October 2026?

Yes, for Capacity Blocks. AWS’s pricing page states that from October 7, 2026, per-accelerator Capacity Block rates rise to $5.970 for P5 (H100), $14.208 for P6-B200 and $16.146 for P6-B300 — about 15% above prior rates. AWS states On-Demand and Savings Plans prices are unchanged.

...

Collection. On October 2, 2026, Axis Intelligence Research read published GPU prices from: Lambda, Runpod and CoreWeave pricing pages; Google Cloud’s accelerator-optimized VM pricing page (us-central1); Microsoft’s Azure Retail Prices API (Standard_ND96isr_H100_v5, East US); AWS’s EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML pricing page; NVIDIA’s January 6, 2025 press release (launch prices); and Newegg search results sorted by lowest price (street prices).

GPU cloud pricing updates monthly and sometimes weekly; marketplace platforms like Vast.ai can change hourly. The rates above were verified in September 2026 – re-check primary pricing pages before you deploy anything.

...

### H100 pricing per hour

An H100 costs $2.89 per hour on RunPod and up to $12.29 on Azure, as of September 2026. That is a more than 4x spread between the cheapest specialist cloud and the most expensive hyperscaler for the same chip. Hostinger doesn’t offer an H100; the B200 covers its top tier.

- RunPod:$2.89 (PCIe); $3.29 (SXM); $3.19 (NVL).
- Lambda:$3.29 (PCIe); from $3.99 (SXM; cheapest per-GPU at the 8-GPU config, single GPU available at $4.29).
- Nebius:$3.85.
- DigitalOcean:$4.41.
- AWS p5.4xlarge:$6.88 (single H100 SXM5; no minimum node).
- Azure NC H100 v5:$6.98 (NVL form factor, single GPU).
- GCP A3 (a3-highgpu-8g): from $11.06 per GPU (8-GPU minimum on-demand).
- Azure ND H100 v5:$12.29 per GPU ($98.32 for the 8-GPU node).

...

### B200 and H200 pricing

The B200 costs $4.50 per hour on Hostinger, $6.79 on RunPod, from $4.38 on Vast.ai, and from $6.69 on Lambda. The H200 starts at $3.87 on Vast.ai and $4.59 on RunPod. GCP’s A4 series starts around $16.11 per GPU-hour but requires a reservation. There’s no standard on-demand option.

The H200 (141 GB HBM3e, a high-bandwidth memory type) carries roughly 75% more VRAM than the H100; RunPod lists it at $4.59. GCP’s A3 Ultra and Azure’s ND H200 v5 also require reservations and aren’t available on standard on-demand.

Both cards sit above the H100, but in different ways: the B200 is a new architecture with higher throughput, while the H200 keeps the H100’s compute and adds memory. As these cards become more widely available, H100 on-demand rates are likely to keep falling. A100 pricing has already dropped below $1 per hour on some marketplace providers as the market shifts toward newer GPU generations.

results.title: What an H100 hour lists for at Azure and Oracle, next to the rental marketplaces (with the VM named) - Show and Tell - Hugging Face Forums
highlights:
“From $X per GPU-hour” is the number everyone quotes for the big clouds, usually without saying which machine you have to rent to get it. I added two clouds whose price lists can be read without an account — Azure and Oracle Cloud — to the rental prices we already collect hourly, and kept the machine attached to every number.

One reading, 2 Oct 2026, 13:00 UTC, USD per GPU-hour:

| GPU | Vast.ai median (offers) | RunPod from | Azure from | Oracle Cloud from |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A100 | 0.74 (58) | 1.39 | 3.40 — ND96asr v4, 8 × 40 GB, VM 27.20/h | 3.05 — BM.GPU4.8, 8 × 40 GB, machine 24.40/h |
| H100 | 2.27 (8) | 2.69 | 6.98 — NC40ads H100 v5, 1 × 94 GB | 10.00 — BM.GPU.H100.8, 8 × 80 GB, machine 80.00/h |
| H200 | 5.12 (7) | 3.59 | 10.60 — ND96isr H200 v5, 8 × 141 GB, VM 84.80/h | 10.00 — BM.GPU.H200.8, 8 × 141 GB, machine 80.00/h |
| B200 | 7.81 (6) | 5.98 | not listed as its own size | 14.00 — BM.GPU.B200.8, 8 × 180 GB, machine 112.00/h |

Three things the table shows at this reading:

1. The per-GPU price hides the unit of sale. Azure’s H100 at 6.98 is a one-card VM you can take alone. Oracle’s 10.00 exists only as an eight-card bare-metal machine at 80.00 an hour. For the A100 both clouds’ lowest per-GPU price sits in an eight-card machine with the 40 GB card; a single 80 GB A100 on Azure lists at 3.67.
2. The gap to the marketplace is larger on the two older cards. List price against the Vast.ai median of the same hour: A100 4.6× (Azure) and 4.1× (Oracle), H100 3.1× and 4.4×; H200 about 2× for both, B200 1.8× (Oracle). One reading, and the marketplace side is thin for the newer classes (six to eight offers) — a description of today, not a trend.
3. The two clouds do not rank the same way per class. Oracle is below Azure on the A100 and the H200, above it on the H100.

What it does not say: availability (a list price is not free capacity), what you pay with a commitment or a negotiated rate, or that a cloud VM and a marketplace host are the same product — they are not; the table compares prices, nothing else.

How the numbers are made: Azure publishes whole-VM prices per region, so the per-GPU price is the Linux pay-as-you-go price divided by the GPU count from Microsoft’s size documentation, lowest across documented sizes and public regions; sizes the price list carries but the documentation does not describe are left out rather than guessed. Oracle prices a GPU-hour directly and has one list without regions. Both are read four times a day and shown beside the marketplace medians, never blended into them.

results.title: H100 Price per Hour in 2026: $1.25 to $11.07 | Opengrid
highlights:
The H100 price per hour depends almost entirely on who you rent it from. On 19 September 2026, on-demand list prices for the same NVIDIA H100 ranged from $1.25 to $11.07 per GPU-hour across twelve providers we looked at, according to getdeploying.com. That is a gap of nearly 9× for the same chip.

...

A note on dates: every price here is a snapshot. On-demand list prices are from getdeploying.com on 19 Sep 2026, and SKUs vary by provider (interconnect, memory, node size). GPU prices move by double digits in weeks, so treat these numbers as a guide to the shape of the market, not a quote.

## H100 on-demand prices by provider

| Provider | Tier | H100 on-demand, $ per GPU-hour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Google Cloud | Hyperscaler | $11.07 |
| Oracle | Hyperscaler | $10.00 |
| Azure | Hyperscaler | $6.98 |
| AWS | Hyperscaler | $6.88 |
| CoreWeave | Neocloud | $6.16 |
| Crusoe | Neocloud | $3.90 |
| Nebius | Neocloud | $3.85 |
| Lambda | Neocloud | $3.29 |
| RunPod | Developer cloud / marketplace | $2.89 |
| Together | Developer cloud / marketplace | $1.99 |
| Vast.ai | Developer cloud / marketplace | $1.79 |
| Lium | Developer cloud / marketplace | $1.25 |

Source: getdeploying.com, 19 Sep 2026. On-demand list prices. SKUs vary by provider.

...

## H100 vs other GPUs: the price bands

The H100 is not the only chip with a wide spread. Thunder Compute's September 2026 data shows the same pattern across the A100, H200 and B200:

| GPU | Price range, $ per hour |
| --- | --- |
| A100 | $1.09 to $5.07 |
| H100 | $2.89 to $11.06 |
| H200 | $3.44 to $10.60 |
| B200 | $3.50 to $27.04 |

Source: Thunder Compute, Sep 2026.

You may notice the H100 low end here ($2.89) is higher than the $1.25 in the provider table above. The two come from different sources, on different dates, covering different sets of providers. They don't contradict each other. They show that the answer to "what does an H100 cost?" depends on whose list you check and when.

Each GPU type also moves on its own. During one stretch, H100 rental prices rose 10% while A100 and B200 stayed flat. The cheapest chip for your job this month is not guaranteed to be the cheapest next month.

results.title: Your Azure Budget Can Change Overnight. Your 2027 Planning Shouldn't. - GenioCT
results.author: Jeremy Genicot
highlights:
This year that scenario is on the calendar. On 8 July 2026 Microsoft announced that it would “transition to annual local currency pricing updates every January for its Commercial Cloud services”. The next update takes effect on 1 January 2027, and detailed guidance follows in November 2026. Product specific price adjustments are still communicated separately.

To be clear: Microsoft has not announced a single percentage increase for all Azure services in January 2027. What changes, and by how much, depends on the products, the purchasing arrangement, the contract and the currencies involved.

...

## 1 February 2027: a regional increase that does come with numbers

January is not the only date. Azure Service Health is now sending affected customers an action required notice, “Prepare for specific Azure VM series and Azure Storage service price updates in seven Azure regions globally”. From 1 February 2027, prices for specific Virtual Machine series and Storage services increase in seven regions:

| Region | Increase |
| --- | --- |
| EU West (Amsterdam) | 9% |
| EU North (Dublin) | 17% |
| France Central | 11% |
| France South | 11% |
| Norway East | 9% |
| Norway West | 9% |
| Southeast Asia (Singapore) | 8% |

The notice also lists what is excluded. On the compute side that includes the v1 series, the v2 series such as Av2, Dv2, Dsv2 and Fsv2, and the new v7 series. On the storage side it excludes, among others, General Block Blob, Standard Page Blob, Tables, Queues, Storage Bandwidth and the Transaction Optimized SKU.

...

Microsoft documents that Azure is priced in US dollars under the Microsoft Customer Agreement and the Microsoft Partner Agreement. The monthly cost is calculated in USD and converted to the billing currency at a rate fixed at the end of the previous month. Enterprise Agreements price Azure in local currency under their own terms.

...

Governator records the January 2027 local currency update without giving it a percentage. Until a figure is published or contractually confirmed, it shows as a known change with an unknown size. It changes no amount and lowers the forecast’s confidence.

highlights:
| When | What happened | Move | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5 Jun 2025 | AWS cuts its H100 on-demand price in a single announcement | −44% | AWS, via CloudZero and IntuitionLabs |
| Jun to Jul 2025 | Other providers follow with their own cuts, in single moves | −20% to −25% | CloudZero, IntuitionLabs |
| Oct 2025 to Mar 2026 | One-year H100 contract price climbs from $1.70 to $2.35 per GPU-hour | about +40% | SemiAnalysis |
| Dec 2025 to Jan 2026 | Silicon Data H100 rental index rises from $2.00 to $2.20 in four weeks | +10% | Silicon Data |
| 2026 | On-demand capacity sold out across all GPU types | n/a | SemiAnalysis |

...

On 5 June 2025, AWS cut its H100 on-demand price by 44% in a single announcement. That is not a gradual drift. It is nearly half the price, overnight, from the largest cloud provider in the world.

Other providers did not wait long. Through June and July 2025, several cut their own prices by 20% to 25%, again in single moves rather than small steps.

...

## Late 2025 into 2026: the reversal

Then the direction flipped.

- Contract prices rose about 40%. SemiAnalysis tracked one-year H100 contracts rising from $1.70 to $2.35 per GPU-hour between October 2025 and March 2026.
- The rental index jumped 10% in four weeks. Silicon Data's H100 rental index went from $2.00 to $2.20 between December 2025 and January 2026.
- Capacity dried up. SemiAnalysis reported on-demand sold out across all GPU types in 2026, and Thunder Compute reports most new NVIDIA allocation is reserved into 2027.

...

## Each GPU moves on its own

It is tempting to think of "GPU prices" as one number. They are not. During the same stretch where the H100 rental index rose 10%, A100 and B200 prices stayed flat (Silicon Data).

Every GPU type has its own price band, and the bands are wide. Thunder Compute's September 2026 data:

| GPU | Price range, $ per hour |
| --- | --- |
| A100 | $1.09 to $5.07 |
| H100 | $2.89 to $11.06 |
| H200 | $3.44 to $10.60 |
| B200 | $3.50 to $27.04 |

Source: Thunder Compute, Sep 2026.

So "is now a good time to rent?" has no single answer. It depends on the chip, the provider and the pricing tier. For a provider-by-provider breakdown, see H100 price per hour in 2026.

results.title: GPU Cloud Pricing Gap Reaches 141% Between Providers | TechSignal.news
highlights:
GPU cloud pricing has diverged into two distinct markets. In late September, the median on-demand NVIDIA H100 price across 40 providers reached $3.42 per GPU-hour, up 15% year over year. But the reported gap between hyperscalers and specialist GPU clouds now reaches 58% for H100s, 81% for B200s, and 141% for H200s. A continuously running 64-GPU H100 cluster at median pricing costs approximately $1.92 million annually before storage, networking, or software.

AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud maintain price premiums through integrated networking, identity management, compliance tooling, and procurement integration. Specialist providers including Vultr, RunPod, and Vast.ai compete on raw compute price and bare-metal performance. The economics now force a workload-specific choice: hyperscalers where integration and data locality justify the premium, neoclouds for cost-sensitive batch inference and training where orchestration complexity is manageable.

B200 capacity pricing reached $5.62 per GPU-hour, up 27.6% year to date. Enterprises comparing only instance prices understate total expenditure. A 64-GPU deployment represents roughly $1.9 million per year in compute alone, making reserved or dedicated capacity economically necessary for sustained workloads.

# ⚠️ Azure pricing update coming in 2027 | Avihai Hajaj ☁ · LinkedIn · 2026-10-04T00:00:00+00:00

**Avihai Hajaj ☁**: Co-founder and CTO @ CloudEdge | Microsoft MVP | Driving Growth Through Cutting-Edge Technologies.

---

⚠️ Azure pricing update coming in 2027

I received a Microsoft notification today about upcoming Azure pricing changes and my first thought was: this is something worth looking at now rather than waiting until February 2027. Starting February 1, 2027, Microsoft will increase pricing for specific Azure VM series and Storage services in seven regions:

☆ North Europe (Dublin) - 17%
☆ France Central / South - 11%
☆ West Europe - 9%
☆ Norway East / West - 9%
☆ Southeast Asia - 8%
The 17% increase in North Europe definitely stands out.

From my perspective, the interesting part isn't just the price increase itself. It's what this means for architecture and FinOps decisions.

Before February, I'd recommend reviewing:
🔹 Current VM and Storage usage by region
